To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single i.p injection of STZ induces progressive NIDDM only in the ICR and ddY mice.
slowly progressive NIDDM was only induced in 125 mg/kg ddY and 125 mg ICR mice by a single administration of a subdiabetic dose of STZ.
the progressive NIDOM is induced by the administration of a subdiabetic dose of STZ in 8-week-old mice, and that the progression of diabetes in the ICR mice is slower than that in the ddY mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of NIDDM induced by a single injection of a sublethal dose of STZ in mice.
the induction of slowly progressive NIDDM in mice by a single i. p. injection of a low dose of STZ, which is different from the conventional model of STZ-induced diabetes.
the induction of slowly progressive NIDDM in ddY and ICR mice, which may be useful in the investigation of NIDDM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 125 mg kg STZ ddY mouse is the most suitable model for slowly progressive NIDDM.
the progressive NIDOM is induced by the administration of a low dose STZ in ICR mice.
the diabetogenic effects of STZ are dependent on both the dose and the strain of the mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a slowly progressive NIDDM can be induced by the administration of a subdiabetic dose of STZ to ICR and ddY, but not to BALB/c and/or C57BL/ 6 mice.
the diabetogenic effects of STZ in mice are different among the strains.
the progressive NIDDBM induced by low-dose STZ is a strain-dependent phenomenon, and that the ddY mouse may be a useful model for slowly progressive NIDDM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diabetogenic effect of STZ varies depending on the mouse strain and that the ddY strain is more sensitive to STZ than the ICR strain.
the progressive NID-DM induced by low dose STZ is a unique phenomenon in ICR and ddY mice, and that the rate of the progression is faster in the ddY mice than that in the ICR mice.
there were differences in the diagenetic activity of STZ in ddY, ICR, BALB/cJ, and C57BL mice.
